subject: RFI: Model inventory, attribution controls and update cadence
messages:
From: Randy Patel <randy.patel@globex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@globex.com
Date: 2026-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: model inventory and attribution controls — clarification request

Marissa,

Thanks for taking this RFI. Attached is the questionnaire our security & procurement teams compiled; a few items we want to clarify up-front:

- We want a per-model inventory that calls out license (OS/CL/other), source citation, and the most recent upstream commit SHA you used to build any served variant. Is that feasible to provide at a per-model level?
- For open-model attribution we ask for a short-form attribution text we can surface in product UI and a longer attribution for legal/compliance records. Can Redwood provide both?
- How do you handle pinning vs. auto-updates? If a model owner publishes a security patch, what is your policy for applying updates to hosted endpoints vs. dedicated/private deployments?

Please mark any items that require redlines or an NDA-first exchange. We would like a response by end of next week to keep the procurement timeline.

Randy
Randy Patel
Senior Security Engineer, Globex Corporation
Randy.Patel@globex.com
Attachment: globex_model_rfi_2026.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Randy Patel <randy.patel@globex.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-21T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: model inventory and attribution controls — initial response

Randy — thanks for the clear list. We've started filling the spreadsheet; primary answers below and I've attached a workbook with per-model rows. Quick summary:

1) Per-model inventory and provenance
- We can provide a CSV/XLSX with model name, public license, upstream source URL, upstream release tag/commit SHA (where available), and the Redwood-verified build artifact ID.
- For models we fork/quantize we include an explicit mapping to the upstream release + our buildstamp. See attached sheet tab "Inventory 2026-Q3."

2) Attribution
- Short attribution (UI): "Model: <model-name> — provided by Redwood Inference (open-source license as noted)"
- Long attribution (legal): a two-paragraph template that includes upstream author, license link, and our buildstamp. We'll include both templates in the attached workbook under tab "Attribution Templates."

3) Pinning and updates
- Hosted (Redwood API): customers may choose an immutable pinned model version (recommended for stability) or a channel (e.g., stable/latest) that receives vetted upstream updates. Default for new endpoints is pinned to the model version used at creation.
- Dedicated / Private: by default we do not auto-apply upstream model updates; customers control rollouts. We offer an automated patch channel for critical security fixes if both parties opt in.
- When upstream publishes a security patch we: (a) generate an internal CVE-impact assessment, (b) publish recommended update notes and test vectors to the customer console, and (c) offer a one-click upgrade path for dedicated/private deployments.

4) Items that may need legal review
- If Globex requires attribution language beyond the short/long templates (e.g., branding placement, additional copyright notices) please flag specific phrasing.

Deliverables attached: redwood_model_inventory_2026.xlsx (contains inventory + templates).

We can formalize this into an answered RFI PDF and include signed attestation for provenance on request. Want me to prepare the signed PDF for procurement?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood_model_inventory_2026.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Randy Patel <randy.patel@globex.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: model inventory and attribution controls — clarification on attribution/legal

Marissa — fyi, looping in Priyom from Product for the pinning/update note and to capture any commercial implications.

Question for legal/product: Globex's procurement team will likely ask for a signed attestation of the provenance fields and a commitment on update cadence (e.g., quarterly vulnerability checks + 30-day response window for critical patches). Can we agree to:

- Provide the signed RFI PDF that enumerates the per-model provenance fields we supplied?
- Commit to quarterly provenance refreshes for hosted models and provide a documented SLA for critical security patches (our proposed: 30 days for patches, expedited if customer opts into emergency patching)?

Marissa, if that commitment lines up with product/ops, I'll include the attestation in the procurement packet and circulate a DocuSign for signature.

-Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Randy Patel <randy.patel@globex.com>
Cc: procurement@globex.com
Date: 2026-07-27T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: model inventory and attribution controls — final answers and attestation

Thanks everyone — finalizing. Short answers and commitments below (this will be the text we include in the signed RFI):

- Inventory: Redwood will deliver the per-model inventory spreadsheet (attached) that includes: model identifier, upstream source URL, upstream release tag/commit, license type, Redwood buildstamp and artifact ID, and field-level provenance notes.
- Attribution: We provide two templates — a short UI string and a longer legal attribution. Both are included; Redwood accepts inclusion of the short UI attribution in Globex product interfaces so long as placement is non-deceptive. Any additional branding requests will require separate approval.
- Pinning & Updates: For hosted APIs, customers can pin a model version; default behavior is pinned at endpoint creation. For Dedicated/Private, Redwood will not auto-upgrade without customer approval. For security vulnerabilities we commit to:
  * Quarterly provenance and vulnerability scans for hosted models in the Redwood model catalog.
  * A 30-calendar-day remediation window for critical patches after Redwood verifies impact, with an option for expedited emergency patching (customer opt-in) within 72 hours.
- Attestation & Sign-off: Redwood will produce a signed RFI PDF (redwood_rfi_answers_signed.pdf) containing the inventory and the above commitments. Once Globex confirms, we will send the DocuSign packet for Marissa to sign.

Related links & artifacts: Drive folder with detailed manifests: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cREDWOOD-GLOBEX-RFI
DocuSign for procurement: https://app.docusign.com/embeddedSigning/abcd-1234-globex-rfi

Randy/procurement — next steps: please confirm the acceptance text for the UI attribution placement and tell us if you need any additional legal language so our legal team can prepare redlines. If all good, Aditya will initiate DocuSign and I will sign the attestation.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood_rfi_answers_signed.pdf (pdf); provenance_manifest_2026.json (json)
